papers.summary: Minic's 2020 talk write-up (Belgrade, Sept. 2019). In it the dual fields Ã of the Standard Model, written as L̃_dm(Ã), are proposed as the dark matter sector (§5, §6.2). In §3 x̃ is the rescaled momentum p/b at ℏ; in the metaparticle it is a λ²-conjugate doubled coordinate. Coupling: a shared metric at zeroth order in λ, plus a Berry-phase-like entanglement term, 'should be detectable'. A conditional explanation of past nulls. Surprising passages: §3 calls fields 'electric' and their duals 'magnetic', and says the chiral doubling keeps the degrees-of-freedom count. Vacuum selection by Born reciprocity is posed as a question. The paper cites the school's MDM series [12] for the dark-matter clause.

answers.question: Q1
answers.answer: Yes, as a proposal or candidate, never derived, from February 2020 on and always at leading order in λ after integrating out x̃. The paper with the most explicit content is Berglund, Hübsch and Minic 2021: 'dark matter … comes from the degrees of freedom dual to the visible matter' (abstract) and 'the dual matter degrees of freedom naturally appear as dark matter candidates' (§5). Others: Minic 2020 §6.2, 'The proposal here is that the dual sector … should be interpreted as the dark matter sector'; EMT 2021 §4, 'which we propose'; BHM 2023 IJMPD §4.3 'good candidates' and §6.4 'a dual Standard Model describing dark matter'; BHM 2023 Symmetry, 'a candidate dark matter companion'; HM 2024 §3.3, 'We will argue'; HM April 2026, 'model (fuzzy) dark matter'; HM October 2026, 'a candidate for the invisible matter sector'. Weaker: Snowmass 2022, 'should be viewed as a dual SM'; BFHKLMM 2022, 'could be associated'; JKMT 2020, 'can be naturally related'; Minic 2023, 'natural candidates'. The nearest wording to 'conjugate matter' is BHM 2023 IJMPD §6.4: the dual particles are 'conjugate to the Standard Model particles in analogy with the canonical fact that momenta p are conjugate to coordinates q'. That is a conjugacy in field space. The school has other candidates too. FKLM 2021 proposes class II metaparticles as 'remnants', hedged as 'dark matter/energy'. The MDM papers of 2010–2018 have non-local quanta obeying infinite statistics, and in 2016–2017 suggest metaparticles as their model (precursors, Q11). The CDM–MOND 'duality' of 2010 and 2014 is a word collision.
evidence: 2202.05104 'Constraints on the nature of dark matter'

answers.question: Q2
answers.answer: The school's own texts give three senses. (i) Foundations, from the modular (Zak) representation of ordinary QM: x̃ is momentum rescaled at ℏ. Minic 2020 §3 and EMT 2021 §2.2 write x ≡ q/a, x̃ ≡ p/b with ab = 2πℏ; FLM 2016 §1.1 writes x̃ ≡ p/ε with λε = 2πℏ and [x̂, x̂̃] = (i/2π)δ; HM 2024 §3.3 writes x̃ ≡ p/ε with [x, x̃] = i and λε = ℏ; Minic 2023 §2 calls the momenta p 'dual coordinates conjugate to x'. This is the canonical conjugate in one phase space, as in #11. (ii) The metastring and metaparticle, where all the dark-matter statements are made: x̃ is an independent doubled coordinate, x̃ = x_L − x_R, the 'canonically conjugate dual space' of BHM 2019 footnote 4. The commutator is 2πiλ² (BHM 2019, 2021), iπλ² with λ² = ℏα′ (FKLM 2021, Minic 2023), iλ² (HM 2024, 2026), or il_P² and iℓ_s² (BHM 2023 Symmetry). Momenta are separate: [x, p] = iℏ = [x̃, p̃], [p, p̃] = 0 (HM 2024 §3.3; BHM 2023 eqs. 3.1–3.2), and (x, x̃, p, p̃) are independent combinations of left and right movers (FLM 2017). λ is the string length ('such as the Planck scale'; 'a new phenomenological scale'). (iii) Field space, surprising: 'the fields and their duals are “canonically conjugate” like q and p … the two form an effective Heisenberg algebra' (BHM 2023 IJMPD §6.4), induced from [x, x̃]; visible φ and dark φ̃ 'do not commute' (HM 2024, 2026). FLM 2014's Y is the string coordinate whose quasi-period is p, 'coordinates in momentum space'. 1801.00160 describes metaparticles as 'two entangled particles in momentum space'.

answers.question: Q3
answers.answer: A dual copy of the whole Standard Model, field by field: 'bi-local extensions of all Standard Model fields' (Minic 2020 §5); 'the entire SM would have a dual SM' (EMT 2021); 'every Standard Model particle has a dual fuzzy counterpart' (HM 2026a). Named partners: a dual photon correlated with ours and 'distinct from the dark photon of effective field theory'; a dual Z; a dual QCD; a dual neutrino in a seesaw; a dual Higgs, possibly the inflaton; a dual axion suited to fuzzy dark matter; a dual gravity sector giving dark energy (BHM 2021 §5; BHM 2023 §6.4–§6.5; HM 2026a). In the heterotic version the dark sector comes from 'the other E8', the Langlands or electric–magnetic dual (BHM 2021 mirror; BHM 2023 Symmetry; HM 2024). Light dual degrees of freedom act as dark radiation (BHM 2023 §6.4). No dual charges are stated. Flag: Minic 2020 §3 says the chiral doubled formulation 'keeps the total number of degrees of freedom the same as in the purely electric formulation', and the founding metaparticle paper says its entanglement 'prevents an interpretation as two particle species'. Neither is reconciled with the separate dark-matter Lagrangian (my reading).

answers.question: Q4
answers.answer: At zeroth order in λ the two sectors share only the metric. In S_eff = ∫√(g g̃)[R + R̃ + L_m(A) + L̃_dm(Ã)], integrating x̃ puts both on √−g(x), with the gravitational background treated as non-dynamical (Minic 2020 eqs. 49–50; BHM 2021 eq. 8). BHM 2023 IJMPD says that 'to first order in the fundamental length, we can treat them as independent'. Beyond that order: (a) a 'mixing/correlation' term from the λ² p dp̃/dτ symplectic term, λ²[[A, Ã]], with F F̃ and ∂A ∂̃Ã cross terms before the x̃-integration. After it the term is (λ⁸/L¹⁰) f [[A, Ã]] (BHM 2021) or (λ₄²/L⁴) 𝓕 [[A, Ã]] (BHM 2023), with a fermion–dual-fermion mass mixing (λ⁹/L¹⁰ or λ₄³/L⁴) that gives a seesaw. It is 'invisible in effective field theory', 'vanishes as either λ → 0 or L → ∞', yet is 'finite even in the limit of zero momenta (deep infrared)'; 'the dark matter sector provides “sources” for the visible matter sector'. (b) A Berry-phase-like entanglement, α′A dÃ/dt (Minic 2020). (c) Non-commuting visible and dual fields, forming 'an effective Heisenberg algebra'. (d) The astrophysical MDM correlation through Λ (a₀ ~ cH₀). What 'correlated' means: 'These fields are in general correlated, due to their non-commutativity' (BHM 2023 §6.3). The strength is not computed: λ₄ and L are 'left unspecified'. FKLM 2021: the dual degrees of freedom 'decouple' at late times. No paper says 'gravity only' or 'kinetic mixing' (0 hits). Contrast: #11 P4 strict, ε ≲ 10⁻¹³.

answers.question: Q5
answers.answer: The school expects detection and explains past nulls only conditionally; no paper states a permanent null. Expected detection: 'dark matter quanta should be detectable through their particular metaparticle entanglement to visible matter' (Minic 2020 §5; EMT 2021 §4). Collider signatures: a dual photon and dual Z, and 'correlated events in the accelerators … not products of any standard particle decays' (BHM 2021 §5; BHM 2023 §6.5); HMN 2012 expects 'dramatic signatures in high energy particle experiments'. The MDM papers (2016, 2017) plan tests 'at colliders, dark matter direct detection experiments and indirect detection experiments'. BHM 2023 footnote 32 says the 'usual detection analysis of particulate dark matter should be revisited'. Nulls: 'If the quanta of modified dark matter are metaparticles, this may explain why, so far, dark matter detection experiments have failed' (Minic 2020; EMT 2021; MDM 2017 abstract, through non-particle phenomenology). Astrophysics: the acceleration scale a₀ ≈ cH₀/2π, the baryonic Tully–Fisher and Faber–Jackson relations and Milgrom scaling, offered as evidence of the visible–dark correlation (HM 2024 §3.4; HM 2026a §5.1; MDM papers; 2009.12915). The search terms for 'null result' gave 0 hits. Contrast: #11 §13 row 7, 'Permanent null'.

answers.question: Q6
answers.answer: Dark matter gravitates on the observed metric. After the x̃-integration, L̃_dm(Ã(x)) sits on √−g(x) beside L_m (Minic 2020 eq. 50; BHM 2021 eq. 8; BHM 2023 eq. 6.19), as #11 §8 has χ propagating on g. Newton's constant comes from the dual space: 'the x̃-integration in the first term defines the gravitational constant G_N' and 'the weakness of gravity is determined by the size of the canonically conjugate dual space, while the smallness of the cosmological constant is given by its curvature' (BHM 2019; BHM 2021 §2; Minic 2020 §6.1). There is a dual gravity sector, and 'the observed gravity and dark energy are correlated via the scale of non-commutativity' (BHM 2021 §4). FLM 2014: GR's flat momentum space 'explicitly breaks' Born's symmetry. The program has no counterpart for G_N from the dual volume.

answers.question: Q7
answers.answer: None of the 41 papers has a velocity-dependent self-interaction or a dependence on relative velocity or momentum overlap: 0 hits for 'relative velocit', and 'velocity depends' occurs only for the Tully–Fisher asymptote. None has localization in x̃ or momentum (0 hits). Self-interaction appears only as an open question ('How does MDM self-interact?', 2016 and 2017), and EMT 2021 §6.2 assumes collisionless dark matter for a turbulence analogy. A fuzzy, wave form is proposed: 'dark matter is fuzzy from the point of view of classical spacetime', because visible and dual fields do not commute (HM 2024 §3.3); 'Metaparticles can be understood as fuzzy dark matter' (§3.4); the quantum pressure ties it to a₀ (HM 2026a §5.1); EEMT 2024 uses standard ultralight fuzzy dark matter. Other dynamics: MDM quanta obey infinite statistics (HMN 2012); light dual degrees of freedom act as dark radiation; dual degrees of freedom dominate early (BHM 2023 §4.3). 'Condensate' hits are unrelated (tachyon condensation, a neutrino-mass fermion condensate). Against #11: χ's gated self-force (§8) is absent. The school's fuzzy form is nearest #11 §12's X-condensate.

answers.question: Q8
answers.answer: No magnetically charged or dyonic dark matter appears in the 41 papers, and nothing is localized in x̃ or momentum. The 'monopole' and 'dyon' hits fall into four groups. (i) On the worldsheet, vertex operators with dual momenta carry 'magnetic charges (dyons)', and DSZ quantization is the diffeomorphism constraint (FLM 2014; 'dyonic states', FLM 2015); the record has this. (ii) In QFT, fields are called 'electric' and their duals 'magnetic', in quotation marks (Minic 2020 §3; EMT 2021 §2.2); these duals are the later dark-matter fields. Not in the record, and a lead for C4. (iii) For gauge groups, Ẽ8 is E8's Langlands, 'electro-magnetic', dual, with 'dark' dual fields (BHM 2021 mirror; BHM 2023 §6.6); the record has this. (iv) Analogies: the x–x̃ algebra is compared to electromagnetism with monopoles or the lowest Landau level (FLM 2017 footnote 10; Minic 2020 footnote 12). In 2212.06086 the hits are reference titles only.

answers.question: Q9
answers.answer: FLM: spacetime is a choice of polarization, a preferred one breaks Born duality, the breaking by GR is 'kinematical' and different from 'dynamical' breaking, and the choice is 'a dynamical question' (FLM 2014, 2015). In QM all polarizations are 'unitarily equivalent' (FLM 2016), T-dualities 'change the choice of polarization' (FLM 2017 JHEP), and as R → 0 the dual-spacetime description takes over (FLM 2017 PRD). So the other choice is equally lawful, as in #11 P5. Selection: worldsheet locality selects the target-space locality condition (FLM 2015 §7); 'quantum gravity picks' or selects the spacetime basis (HM 2024; HM 2026a); Minic 2020 §7 asks whether Born reciprocity can be a vacuum-selection criterion. Surprising: FKLM 2021 says the dual Lorentz symmetry is 'fundamentally broken at the quantum level', that 'The symmetry breaking happens at the level of the vacuum sector, and thus a choice of ground state fixes' δ (and with it which commuting coordinate is spacetime), and proposes 'the expansion of the Universe' as 'a mechanism that selects the decoupling frame'. BHM 2023 §4.3 calls O(1,d−1)₂ 'effectively spontaneously broken'. No paper writes a potential, an order parameter η or a Goldstone mode (0 hits); the breaking is never of ρ itself. The 'vacuum selection' of Snowmass 2022 is landscape selection, a word collision.

answers.question: Q10
answers.answer: At leading order dark energy is a positive cosmological constant, w = −1, from the curvature of the dual spacetime, with a seesaw M_Λ ~ M²/M_P (BHM 2019; Minic 2020 §6; BHM 2021). Here w is pressure over energy density. Beyond leading order it is time-dependent, from the 'dynamical geometry of the dual spacetime' (JKMT 2020). The sign of the deviation changed. JKMT 2022 gave 'w_eff < −1 in this framework' (bounded so that w_eff ≤ −1), a phantom against #11 §10. Hur et al. 2025 call this 'our first, naive guess'. Their adopted UV–IR relation gives 'w(a) ≥ −1 in all cases' with wₐ < 0 and 'w(a) > −1', compared favourably with DESI. That is the sign pattern of #11 §10's thawing τ (w ≥ −1, wₐ < 0), by another mechanism: dual-curvature quanta with infinite statistics, not hilltop quintessence on the Maslov circle. No paper has a contracting or collapsing dual spacetime that drives our acceleration (C5, App. A item 9). Related passages: the cell rescaling x → ax, x̃ → a⁻¹x̃ ('the dual dimension shrinks') (FKLM 2021; Minic 2023, there with x → ax, p → a⁻¹p), which is App. A item 6's a·ã = 1; 'in the early (small) universe the dual (“dark”) degrees of freedom dominate' (BHM 2023 §4.3); and a 'dual universe made of dual particles' as a → 0 (FKLM 2021).

answers.question: Q11
answers.answer: In these 41 papers the earliest statement that the duals of visible fields are dark matter is Minic 2020 (2020-02-29), §5 and §6.2. Minic 2020 cites its own school: [12], the MDM series including 1709.04388, for 'metaparticle quanta … representing the natural quanta of dark matter', and [89], 'BHM, in preparation', for the action with the dual matter sector. Precursors by the same group, not in the record: 1601.00662 (2016-01-04), where MDM quanta 'could be found in recent reformulations of quantum gravity and string theory' (FLM 2013–2015); 1709.04388 (2017-09-13), where metastring non-local excitations 'can serve as unusual dark matter quanta' and the zero-mode sector 'could be viewed as a model for modified dark matter quanta'; and 1801.00160 (2017-12-30), where MDM quanta 'might be modeled as metaparticles … two entangled particles in momentum space'. None says dark matter is the dual of visible matter. BHM 2023 IJMPD §4.3 cites the unread FLM, IJMPA 34 (2019) 1941004 (not on arXiv), with Minic 2020, for dual particles as dark matter candidates. No paper cites anyone outside the school for the identification. Every paper is before P.R.'s September 2026 notebook except 2610.19522 (2026-10-14).

contradicts_record.source_says: 1709.04388 §5 (posted 2017-09-13, one version): 'We expect that such non-local excitations (as part of a covariant non-commutative formulation, as implied by the metastring [131, 132]) can serve as unusual dark matter quanta.' and 'Roughly, the zero mode sector looks like two entangled particles, and it could be viewed as a model for modified dark matter quanta discussed in this review'. 1801.00160 §5 (2017-12-30): 'Thus, MDM quanta are not particle-like, but might be modeled as metaparticles, excitations of metastrings, which look roughly like two entangled particles in momentum space.' 1601.00662 §4 (2016-01-04): MDM quanta 'could be found in recent reformulations of quantum gravity and string theory (Freidel, Leigh & Minic, 2013; …)'. Minic 2020 §1 cites [12], which lists 1709.04388, for its dark-matter clause. 2212.06086 §4.3 cites [254] (FLM, IJMPA 34 (2019) 1941004) with [255] (Minic 2020) for 'such dual particles appear as good candidates for dark matter'.
contradicts_record.why: The metaparticle-as-dark-matter clause that flag 64 quotes from Minic 2020 appears two and a half years earlier, as a speculation, in two papers of the same group (Edmonds, Farrah, Minic, Ng, Takeuchi), one of which places the two entangled particles 'in momentum space'. Neither says dark matter is the dual of visible matter; in these 41 papers that identification first appears in Minic 2020. So 'one priority, Minic 2020' holds for the dual-of-visible identification but not for the metaparticle clause the flag quotes. The school also credits the unread 2019 FLM paper for the dual-particle candidacy, so that paper's full text could move the priority to 2018–2019 (it is from a conference of February 2018).

contradicts_record.record_says: notes/literature-check.md §3 plain-language passage: the school's dark sector 'is correlated with ours by construction, where the program's couples to ours by gravity alone'; 'What differs': 'Their dual sector is correlated with ours by construction'; wiki/summary.md line 34: 'their sector correlated with ours'.
contradicts_record.source_says: 2212.06086 §6.3: 'These fields are in general correlated, due to their non-commutativity. However, to first order in the fundamental length, we can treat them as independent.' §6.2: 'In general the observed spacetime and its dual are correlated, which should be important for phenomenology, but to first order in the fundamental length we will treat them as independent sectors.' §6.4: the mixing 'is invisible to effective field theory, and it vanishes as either' λ₄ → 0 or L → ∞; footnote 43: 'so here we leave them unspecified'. 2003.00318 eqs. (49)–(50): after the x̃-integration L_m(A(x)) and L̃_dm(Ã(x)) sit on one √g(x) '(where we have included the gravitational background as non-dynamical)'.
contradicts_record.why: 'Correlated' is the school's own word and follows from its construction, but the school puts the correlation beyond leading order. At zeroth order, and in BHM's words to first order in the fundamental length, the visible and dual sectors are independent and share only the metric, as in #11 P4. The non-gravitational pieces are suppressed by powers of λ, invisible in EFT, and vanish as λ → 0 or L → ∞: mixing ∝ λ⁸/L¹⁰ or λ₄²/L⁴, a fermion–dual-fermion mass mixing, and non-commuting fields. Their size is never computed. The contrast with 'gravity alone' is therefore a contrast at sub-leading order, which the record's wording does not say. It understates how close the two are at leading order.

contradicts_record.record_says: notes/literature-check.md §3, 'What their dual is', second bullet: 'The identification matches C1 in their foundations; their model doubles phase space where the program polarizes one.'
contradicts_record.source_says: 2212.06086 §6.4: 'First the fields and their duals are “canonically conjugate” like q and p' … 'the dual particles are conjugate to the Standard Model particles in analogy with the canonical fact that momenta p are conjugate to coordinates q' … 'That is, the dual fields do not commute with Standard Model fields, and the two form an effective Heisenberg algebra.' 2003.00318 §3: 'So even though one has formally doubled the number of variables, the chiral nature of the theory, keeps the total number of degrees of freedom the same as in the purely electric formulation.'
contradicts_record.why: The record finds the match with C1 only in the foundations (x̃ ≡ p/b) and describes the model as a doubling. Yet the section just before the one the record cites for the identification (BHM 2023 IJMPD §6.5) states a conjugacy inside the model itself: the dark (dual) fields are canonically conjugate to the visible fields, as p to q, induced from [x, x̃]. That is a third sense of 'conjugate', in field space, and closer in wording to 'conjugate matter' than anything the record quotes. Minic 2020 §3 adds that the doubled formulation does not double the degrees of freedom. My reading: the record understates the overlap in wording; whether field-space conjugacy is the program's exchange of polarizations is open.
